title: How Icelandic last names work: patronymics, matronymics, phone books and the naming committee

sources.title: Icelandic Naming System: A Unique Tradition in Modern Times
Icelanders can now call their daughters Angelina after official name list expanded
Iceland’s Naming Laws Prevented a 10-Year-Old From Getting a Passport

facts.text: Most Icelanders do not have a family name; family names are rare in Iceland.
An Icelandic last name is usually formed from the father’s first name plus -son for a son or -dóttir for a daughter.
A son and a daughter of the same father therefore have different last names, such as Sigurdsson and Sigurdardottir.
Last names formed from the mother’s first name are also used and are becoming more common.
A person’s patronymic last name stays the same after marriage.
Icelandic telephone directories are arranged alphabetically by first name.
New given names must be approved by Iceland’s Naming Committee, which keeps a list of approved names.
Names that cannot take the case endings of Icelandic grammar are routinely turned down.

notes: 混合題 mixed-top-04 第 4 組（冰島人的命名）用。2026-10-09 線上查證，只取事實、不取原句。Text A 的 Gunnar、Einar、Helga 是說明用的例子；Text B 的 Sigrún Ólafsdóttir 與兒子 Ari Sigrúnarson 是虛構人物（母名＋-son 依 f4），機場盤問、同事稱呼等是個人經驗的文學描寫。
